applicable_when: The kernel performs a large GEMM (M=65536, N=2304, K=768) with ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing all dot-product accumulation through scalar FP32 FFMA units. On H200 SXM5, scalar FP32 peaks at 67 TFLOPS while TF32 Tensor Cores peak at 989 TFLOPS — nearly 15x more throughput. The kernel currently achieves only 37% of scalar FP32 roofline, meaning enabling TF32 would both unlock Tensor Core hardware AND reduce register pressure (Tensor Core instructions are more compact), potentially improving the catastrophic 12.5% occupancy caused by 255 registers/thread. K=768 is moderate enough that TF32 mantissa truncation (23→10 bits) accumulates error well within atol=1e-3 for typical transformer inference/training workloads. The diversity instruction explicitly targets this optimization.

applicable_when: The kernel uses BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32 with FP32 accumulation. The 128x128 FP32 accumulator tile alone requires 16,384 floats x 4 bytes = 65,536 bytes. With 128 threads per block, that is 512 bytes = 128 registers per thread just for the accumulator, plus loop variables and address arithmetic, pushing total register usage to the hardware maximum of 255. This limits occupancy to 12.5% (2 blocks/SM), leaving 87.5% of SM warp slots idle. The B-matrix load uses a complex broadcast_to pattern that causes register spilling to local memory, producing the 1/32-byte utilization in local load/store sectors. The fix is two-fold: (1) reduce BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N to 64 to cut accumulator register demand by 4x, freeing registers for more concurrent warps; (2) replace the manual pointer arithmetic loads with tl.make_block_ptr + tl.load(..., boundary_check=...) to leverage Hopper TMA hardware, eliminate the broadcast_to spill pattern, and enable async pipelining via num_stages>1.
